Tuesdays - granite 170 main room 162 


Tuesday Practice is a welcoming, beginner-friendly space for anyone who is interested in learning music and becoming part of our performance group. No prior musical experience is required—whether you’ve never played an instrument before or you’re simply curious and want to learn, you are encouraged to join us. During these practices, we introduce newcomers to the fundamentals of playing, help students become familiar with the instruments and music, and gradually build their skills and confidence. As students progress, we slowly begin teaching new music and preparing them to eventually participate alongside the performance group. The goal of Tuesday Practice is to create a supportive environment where beginners can learn at their own pace, meet other musicians, and develop the skills needed to perform with the group. Come learn, practice, and grow with us! Everyone is welcome, and no experience is necessary.

# What is ¡Bobcat Nature!?
¡Bobcat Nature! is a unique overnight program for UC Merced students to experience Yosemite park. Participants get guided hikes and activities through select parts of the Valley and a chance to reconnect with nature. Transportation, lodging, and meals are all included!
- Please be ready and at the University Transit Center by **7:15am this Saturday**. We will be back on campus by Sunday afternoon.
- Please bring 100% of the gear you will need! Due to the nature of our trip, **sleeping bags and other hiking essentials are not guaranteed.** Pack clothes, water, sunscreen, bedding, toiletries, and all other items you need for a two-day trip with moderate hiking.

# How do I apply?
Fill out this form: https://forms.gle/2WZkfYMXbeZChnKL7

1. Spots are FIRST COME, FIRST SERVED. Act quickly to secure your spot!
2. **Priority will be given to students that are PAL members on Catlife.** If you are not already a member on Catlife, there are instructions within the form to sign up!
3. Shortly after you complete this form, you will receive a DM from a PAL staff member. This is how we will confirm your eligibility and provide you the official ¡Bobcat Nature! sign-up form. **You are required to fill out both forms to attend this trip!**

Don't hesitate to ask any questions you may have. We're looking forward to seeing you there!

description:
Black Town Hall: “No Cap, Let’s Talk Politics — The Election, the Issues & What It Means for Us” is a civic engagement program hosted by the Phi Alpha Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Incorporated at UC Merced. Open to all students and members of the campus community, the Town Hall creates an engaging space for candid conversations about politics, voting, political representation, and issues affecting Black communities and our broader society. Through a moderated discussion with community leaders, educators, advocates, and professionals, the program will explore how government and public policy impact our everyday lives, the importance of local and national elections, barriers to civic participation, and ways to stay engaged beyond Election Day. Ultimately, the goal is for attendees to leave more informed about the issues, empowered to use their voices, and prepared to advocate for themselves and their communities.

Coming up: Camera Trap Data Processing Workshop

Hi yall, we have some exciting news! We'll be kicking off our Camera Trapping Project series of events this Sunday. If you're interested in seeing cool animals on footage gathered by students and learning how to analyze data in a professional setting, this is the workshop for you.

Place: COB2 110
Date: November 8, Sunday
Time: 12pm - 4pm

Last spring, we set out camera traps to record for two weeks in the land of Merced County Co. Unit 9, a patch of protected vernal pool habitat just west of campus. Our first Camera Trap Data Processing workshop will consist of processing this data, and it will serve as an introductory workshop for the rest of our camera trapping activities this semester. Students will learn how to manage, filter, and identify videos and photos from camera traps. This data will be submitted to the county of Merced to help track and protect our wildlife out in the grasslands and vernal pool habitat of Unit 9!

This is a great way to get your foot in the door with field research and gain experience with real life camera trap processes. This will be a professional-grade event that you can put on your resume, but you are required to attend the full event if you wish to do so. Please bring your laptop and your Catcard/student ID.
